Subject: Commercial readiness & billing start confirmation — HelioSecure discovery follow-up

Hey Rajiv — thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our call: 

Summary of where we landed
- Procurement preference: your team signaled preference for PO (AP workflow) but expressed interest in Marketplace if it shortens procurement cycles.
- Trial goals / success criteria (as discussed):
  1) Sustained usage: >= 50,000 inference tokens/day for 2 consecutive weeks in non-sandbox environment.
  2) Performance: 95th percentile latency < 300ms for your primary workload.
  3) Integration: SSO + service account access for ETL pipeline.
- Billing start options we suggested: start-on-date (we proposed 2027-03-01) or start-on-threshold (billing begins once usage thresholds met).

Open items / asks for HelioSecure
- Procurement route: confirm PO (AP) vs card vs AWS Marketplace. If PO, please share the procurement contact or email (we can route the SOW to them).
- Vendor onboarding: HelioSecure requested SOC 2 evidence and a short vendor questionnaire — attaching a SOC summary and the draft SOW for review.
- Dashboard access: we can provision trial account access and a dashboard to monitor token usage; let us know which user(s) should get access.

Proposed immediate next steps
1) I’ll send the SOW and SOC summary (attached).
2) Please confirm procurement contact and whether you want the Marketplace route — we can engage our partnerships team if so.
3) Marissa will follow up on billing flexibility and invoicing guardrails so your procurement team can understand timing.

Attachments: SOW_HelioSecure_v1.pdf (draft), redwood-soc2-summary.pdf

Thanks — tagging Marissa and Karthik to help with billing/PO logistics.

—Jonas

Appreciate the clear recap. A few quick answers from our side: 
- Procurement route: preference is PO (internal policy) but we are evaluating Marketplace to speed approvals. If Marketplace reduces paperwork on our end, we might push for it. Can Redwood support both routes in parallel?

Thanks for the recap, Jonas — and hi Rajiv, nice to meet you over email. A couple of notes on billing and procurement flexibility from Redwood: 

Billing options we can accommodate
- Option A (calendar start): We can set billing to start on a calendar date you pick (we suggested 2027-03-01). Invoices are issued on that date; if you provide a PO after the start date we can backdate credits to align with the PO.
- Option B (threshold start): We can enable billing to commence automatically when the trial success criteria (usage thresholds) are reached. This is useful if you want to guarantee that you're only charged after the integration is validated.

Marketplace vs PO
- Marketplace: good for faster procurement for some customers; we’ll need to confirm listing availability in your cloud region and whether your finance team accepts marketplace terms. If you want us to triage Marketplace onboarding we can kick our partnerships team.
- PO: standard path; we can accept a PO and hold invoicing until PO is received if that helps your cycles. In practice customers often sign PO + SOW and we enable service immediately with invoicing held for bookkeeping.

Administrative items we can provide now
- Live trial account + usage dashboard (we can provision access within 24 hours once you provide admin emails).
- Completed vendor questionnaire (we’ll send the vendor security questionnaire and a short SOC 2 summary).
- SOW (attached) — we can route to DocuSign once you confirm the procurement contact.

Suggested next steps (concrete)
1) Rajiv — share the procurement contact (name + email) we should route the SOW to.
2) If you want Marketplace investigated, reply and I’ll loop in Partnerships.
3) Confirm which user(s) should receive dashboard access so we can provision accounts.

I’m attaching the SOW_HelioSecure_v1.pdf (draft) and redwood-soc2-summary.pdf for your procurement/security team. Happy to hop on a 20-minute sync with procurement if it helps.

—Marissa
